cohort: The study included 28,176 women aged 15-49 who had singleton births in the past 5 years across Burkina Faso, Gambia, Kenya, Senegal, and Tanzania.
finding: Women who had undergone FGM/C were 31% less likely to have Caesarean sections in singleton births.
mod_finding: Women who had undergone FGM/C were 31% less likely to have Cesarean sections, while higher birth weight and higher education levels for both women and their husbands were associated with increased odds of Caesarean sections.
country: Burkina Faso, Gambia, Kenya, Senegal, Tanzania
cross-section timing: singleton birth in the past 5 years
birth_weight: Higher birth weight was associated with increased odds of Caesarean sections.
